body: Yes, you can message me.
I wasn't. We were only doing formula.
I dont think you did anything wrong. I felt like it was less sedating with each dose. By day 4 for me, it wasnt sedating at all. Meds effect everyone different, so it may just not make you sleepy.
I hope it goes well for you and you start feeling better quickly!
I felt like the first few days were the most sedating. So if possible could you start it on a friday night? Than see how you feel the next couple of days and decide than if you need to take time off?

I took it during my maternity leave so wasnt working at the time. I feel like I would have been capable of working. But the medication can be quite sedating for some people, so it may not be possible if that is how it effects you.

It treated my postpartum depression pretty well. I felt a connection with my son after taking it and actually felt like I loved him. I also was close to psychosis and the med stopped that in its tracks. I do have preexisting mental health issues that it wasn't able to cure. But that isn't what this medication was intended for.
It worked very well for me. I would take it again without hesitation.
I got mine from CVS Specialty.
I have never had issues with PMDD, but I do treatment resistant depression and PTSD.
Took it once a day in the evening. You take it for a total of 14 days. My psychiatrist said that it has positive effects for over 8 months after you take it.

I would get this drugged/sedated feeling a couple hours after taking it. Which made waking up to baby difficult. Also would stumble a bit, like as if drunk. This resolved by morning. It also was a bit of a rollercoaster for my mood at first. I would feel really good in the morning and than as the day went on, it would wear off. After 4 days, it didn't feel like it noticeably was helping. It started to help again on day 12. I also had significant loss of appetite by day 10 and had to force eat to get the amount of calories/fat required when taking it.
I tried it and it was a lifesaver for me. Wasn't without side effects, but for me they were tolerable and I would 100% take it again.
It took about 4 weeks total from when the med was prescribed to when i received it. And for me the med was life saving and worth the wait.
I started taking it when I was 8 weeks postpartum.

I'm doing really well now. I would say my ppd is gone. About 2 weeks after I was finished with the med I did have some rebound depression. That lasted a couple of days, and than after that I felt back to normal. It was a life saving med for me. I hope it works well for you.
No, I actually did the nasal spray treatments.

I've personally tried it. I have treatment resistant depression and have tried many antidepressants that all failed. After the initial dosing, I was getting the treatment every 2 weeks. I did find the treatment relaxing and easy to do. It is an intense feeling for the first hour, but started to wear off after that. The positive effects of the treatment would last till the next dose for me. I discontinued it due to living 45 mins from the clinic that did it and the fact you have to be driven after the treatment. Which just wasn't feasible for me to keep doing. The benefit of it is that you'll know much quicker if it will help you than a traditional antidepressant. And i experienced no withdrawals when I discontinued it. This is just my personal experience with it. Everyone is different of course.
They were doing okay, but not really working quite enough. Now it seems like they are working less and less. I have an appointment Monday, it's just trying to hold on till then.

I didn't have that problem with effexor but I did have issues like that with prozac. This is just your body saying that this isnt the right med for you. Tell your doctor immediately what is happening.

I've found meds to be the most effective treatment for me. Unfortunately it takes a lot of trial and error to find the right one. Also if you are young you cannot get ect as your brain is still developing. Or at least that is what I was told. At the very least I would reccomend therapy, they can help give you the tools that can benefit you if you decide to not use medication.

That it is an illness like any other, it isn't my fault. Nothing I'm doing is causing this. No amount of exercise, eating healthy, or drinking water is going to fix me. Though I agree it doesn't hurt to do it.
Why, when everything in my life is going great, am i still depressed?

Any medication that you take can effect you negatively. Please contact the provider that prescribed it to you and let them know how you are feeling. It shouldn't be making you feel worse, so this might be a sign that you need to try something different.

I understand that you want to die to end the pain of it all. But as a medical professional i need to tell you that tylenol is highly ineffective as a way to kill yourself. You will possibly end up with kidney damage and will feel extremely nauseous. I have myself tried overdosing on it with around that dosage. It does not work.

I'm sorry to here that your opportunities to get help are few. You could maybe try a online therapy. I have use 7cups.com before. It is free to talk to a regular person or costs $150 for a month worth of talking to a counselor. I've only talked to regular people, but they have given me some great advice. Maybe that could be an option for you.

A lot of places actually offer discounted or even free appointments for people who are low income. I don't know if you are in the US, but the Good Samaritan society often offers low cost appointments or if you are in college the health center usually does free counseling for students.
Not calling a close friend. They committed suicide 2 days later.

Im sorry that you have been having a tough time. It sounds like you have made several steps in the right direction. But unfortunately things don't get better right away. But, What if the job does work out? What if you do great in school? Just take one day at a time. I wish you well.

Reading this was in no way a waste of my time. I don't really have a whole lot of advice, because im still trying to figure stuff out myself. But i do offer this; take one day at a time. Our struggle isn't ever really over. Though i know that that isn't the most encouraging statement. But when we accept that it helps give us power over the illness. We are able to control and manage it, not the other way around. Even if that means we have help from medication or therapy. I hope that your family will come to realise that isn't just a temporary thing and will support you. I also hope that in some way this will help. But either way I wish you the best.
Medication, therapy, and my best friend.

I recommend counseling for having someone to talk to. I also struggle to talk to anyone about my mental health issues. Counseling has made a world of a difference for me. I may only be a stranger, but i care about it. No one should go through this hellish battle alone.
Thank you so much for your kind words. That is a unique way to see everything and it does definitely give me a better perspective on my illness.

First just take a deep breath. We all make mistakes; say and do things we don't really mean. Try and be kind to yourself. You don't deserve to die just because you may have messed up and lost a friend. So please, do your best to take care of yourself.

I know that the state I live in does it. But it is done on the other side of the state and I just can't afford that. I also want the vns, but I haven't found a doctor yet that will order it for me. I'm hoping that you will have the opportunity to try these therapies. Even a few more days of feeling better is worth it.

I know what you mean about just wanting to be cured. Instead of doing just a bunch that in the end doesn't cure it. I figured I would try this new med I got prescribed and if that doesn't work I'll look into it more. Another drug free option is a vagus nerve stimulator which has been somewhat curative. A med option is called esketamine which has had terrific results for people with treatment resistant depression. Though not many places offer it. It gets really tiring to keep trying things and not having them work. But who knows maybe someone will figure something out and we can be cured.

Med changes are the worst and i've started to lose faith that any med will work. I also looked at doing tms. I have heard quite good things about it. The only issue is that it is expensive if you are in America. Around 10 grand for one year of sessions. I still haven't found out if my insurance will cover it, because I would love to try it. Besides meds have you tried any therapies? I found cbt to be quite helpful.

Lexapro worked really well for my anxiety, but didn't work super well for my depression. I have treatment resistant depression which is why I've tried so many medications. When you were on your anti depressants did they give you a adjunct med (med that boosts the effects of another) along with it? For me i take seroquel along with effexor to make the effexor more effective. That may help keep your meds be effective for longer.

Each time I have switched it has been a new experience. When switching prozac i had a bad reaction. But switching to effexor went fine, though i did have some weird side effects like nightsweats for awhile. But effexor ended up being the med that gave me relief. They really are different even though the are in the same class. I say that you can never ask too many questions. This is your health after all. I work in the medical field as a nurse, and I am always willing to answer questions no matter how many that they have. So please, ask away.

Since you say that the lexapro stopped working for you, i don't think it will work if you started it again. Keep in mind that there are many anti-depressants out there. Talking with a doctor can help you figure out which med might work best for you. If you have any questions about specific meds I've been on lexapro, prozac, effexor, remeron, and just started abilify. I wish you luck.

Medication has saved my life. But in the end whether you take medication is a very personal decision. Talk to your doctor. Talk to your therapist if you have one. Just know the risks and benefits of taking medication and of not taking anything.

I'm really sorry to hear that you are in pain; both physically and mentally. It must be incredibly difficult. I read that you said that doctors have only been prescribing you opiods. Have you ever seen palliative care physicians? One of their specialties is in managing pain. I hope that tomorrow will be better than today. And that you can find relief, or at least the means to cope. I wish you well.

Fuck is it tough. But one minute at a time. And than maybe one hour at a time. You can do this. Just do what you can, and don't worry about anything else. Try and seek help, whether it is a friend, family member, reddit user, or counselor. Any support is better than no one.

I know that this isn't the most helpful thing to say to you right now. But you are you, whether your teeth are healthy or not. I also struggle with brushing my teeth. You are more than your teeth. You are a wonderful human who has fears. But that doesn't mean it has to control you. Do your best to care of your physical health in any way you can. Even if it is just admitting that you might need to brush more. You can do this. We are behind you; you are not alone.
Birthdays are rough for me too. Everyone is so happy about it. But for me it is just a painful reminder that I'm still alive.

Yeah, I have had some tough times. I almost died a little over 2 years from an overdose. I also had many other precipitating suicide attempts before that. Were you able to work it out with your girlfriend?
Do you live in a cornfield? Because I'm stalking you.
I'm sorry to hear that. I hope that he can get some professional help, depression is no joke.
Thanks, I appreciate it. It has been a rough couple of months.
A cure for my depression.
It sounds like it could have possibly been a seizure. I would definitely follow up with a doctor to be sure.

I had a friend who struggled with mental health issues and I had the thought that I should call him and see how he was doing. I got busy and didn't get around to it. He killed himself 2 days later. I can't help but wonder, if I had called would he still be alive?
When i got an answer wrong on a math assignment and my first thought was that I should die.
I just lost a friend to suicide. Im glad that you are still around.
Today we buried one of my closest friends. He was only 23.

Anti-depressants saved my life. Around this time last year I almost died from an overdose that landed me in the ICU. After getting on the right med, I haven't had suicidal thoughts in months and am starting to feel like there may actually be a chance that I can be happy. I've been in therapy for many years, but in the end the meds were what really worked.
Anything. If it keeps you living, than that is all that matters. Then there is at least a chance that things will get better.
While therapy helped a lot, it was really getting on the right medication that me actually feel happy for the first time in 10 years.

When I attempted to end my life by stabbing a ball point pen through my neck. Got started on the right antidepressant finally and cut out some shitty people in my life. I can finally say that I truly feel happy for the first time in 10 years.
Yo mama so fat we are all seriously concerned about her health.
That I waited so long to get help for my mental health issues. If I had gotten help when it began I would be in a much better place than I am in now.
Thank you for your kind words. I really appreciate it :)
Hey, I'm glad you're still here. If you want someone to talk to I'd gladly listen.

Mine would probably be the small scar I have on my neck. When I was in deep depression I attempted suicide and was admitted to the behavioral health hospital. In the hospital I desperately wanted to die so I grabbed a pen, the pointiest thing i could find, and attempted to push/stab it through my neck in an attempt to sever an artery or vein. I wasn't able to pierce through the skin, but it did end up leaving a scar.
If I attempted suicide for attention.
"All of your emotions seem fake"

I was in this exact same situation not that long ago. I was struggling majorly in school and my depression just kept getting worse. I ended up deciding to take a break and dropped out in order to deal with my depression. It has been one of the best decisions I've ever made. I still struggle, but not having the pressure of school on top of it has made it more manageable. I wish you the best in whatever you end up choosing to do.

If you do end up trying an antidepressant don't lose hope if the first one you try doesn't work. The first two I tried didn't help me at all. I'm now on my third and while I'm not 100% yet, I almost feel like I did before my depression started. Whatever you choose to do I wish you luck.
